questions.title: Which film will win the Special Jury Prize at the 2026 Venice Film Festival?
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The Venice Film Festival’s official announcement of its 2026 award winners. Resolution : Resolve to the film awarded the Special Jury Prize at the 2026 festival, once the winner is publicly announced. Accepted Answer Format : The winning film’s title.
questions.current_reasoning: Breaking Aug 24 announcement: Venice Film Festival organizers added 'NAZA' as a late 21st title in the main Golden Lion competition—the sole documentary in the lineup. Directed by Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor (co-directors of Oscar-winning 'No Other Land') and produced/executive-produced by James Wilson and Jonathan Glazer (the exact team behind 'The Zone of Interest' and last year's Venice Grand Jury Prize runner-up 'The Voice of Hind Rajab'), 'NAZA' premieres late in the festival on Sept 10 before a jury chaired by Maggie Gyllenhaal that also includes 'Hind Rajab' director Kaouther Ben Hania, Johnnie To, and Daniel Blumberg. Because documentaries are rarely awarded Best Director, Screenplay, or Acting prizes, strong jury support concentrates directly on Golden Lion, Grand Jury Prize, and especially the Special Jury Prize (matching Venice's track record for urgent political works like 'Green Border'), vaulting 'NAZA' to #1 at 0.09 (replacing 'The Echo Chamber' in top 5). With the competition expanded to 21 films (uniform baseline 0.048) and no premieres until Sept 2, we trim Lee Chang-dong's 'Possible Love' (0.08 -> 0.07) and Werner Herzog's 'Bucking Fastard' (0.07 -> 0.06) while holding Hirokazu Kore-eda's 'Look Back' (0.07) and May el-Toukhy's 'Woman Unknown' (0.07), leaving 64% across the remaining 16 titles until screenings and reviews begin.

local_articles.title: Films are ‘unavoidably political,’ says Maggie Gyllenhaal at Venice Film Festival
local_articles.snippet: DUBAI: Politics quickly moved to the center of attention at the Venice Film Festival’s jury press conference, where jury president Maggie Gyllenhaal was asked whether cinema has a responsibility to engage with politics. “OK,” Gyllenhaal said with a laugh. “May as well get into it.” The filmmaker, whose latest directorial project is “The Bride,” responded by arguing that politics and cinema are inherently intertwined, describing films as “fundamentally, unavoidably political.” “Look, we could say, how are we possibly here talking about movies right now when the world is in a state of emergency?” she said. “To me, the answer has something to do with empathy. local_articles.title: Clooney honored as Hollywood-light Venice Film Festival kicks off
local_articles.snippet: A smiling George Clooney was honored with a lifetime award at the start of the Venice Film Festival on Wednesday where the long-time Donald Trump critic took another swipe at the US president. The 65-year-old Oscar winner was called a “legend” by actress friend Laura Dern as she presented him with the gong in front of a star-studded audience at the start of the 83rd edition of the festival. Clooney, accompanied by his lawyer wife Amal, was cheered by hundreds of well-wishers on the red carpet, while Dern read out tributes from past co-stars including Brad Pitt and Adam Sandler during the ceremony. “When you start reflecting on the years, you realise you really didn’t have a career as much as a series of happy accidents,” Clooney told the audience. local_articles.title: Venice Film Festival to hand actor George Clooney lifetime achievement award on opening night
local_articles.snippet: VENICE – The Venice Film Festival kicks off on the sun-splashed Lido with a bang on Sept 2, with the glamorous cinema showcase handing George Clooney a lifetime achievement award on its opening night. The charismatic 65-year-old – a frequent red carpet guest at the world’s oldest film festival – will provide a shot of A-list adrenaline despite Hollywood studios mostly staying away in 2026. But while the festival may lack mass-market blockbusters, there is no shortage of larger-than-life subjects, with films about Elon Musk, Rupert Murdoch and the volatile Gallagher brothers from the Britpop band Oasis on the calendar. questions.title: Who will top the PSA women's world squash rankings on September 21, 2026?
questions.background: The Professional Squash Association (PSA) publishes weekly world rankings for professional squash players.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The official PSA women's world rankings dated September 21, 2026. Resolution : Resolve to the player ranked first in that rankings update. Accepted Answer Format : The player's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Official August 2026 PSA Squash Tour and Gulf Times draw releases clarify that TWO major ranking events occur before the Sept 21 rankings update (rather than one as assumed in June): the Gold-level London Squash Classic (Sept 1-6) and the Platinum-level QTerminals Qatar Classic (Sept 12-18). World No. 1 Hania El Hammamy remains favored (90.4% win rate in 2025/26, defending 2025 Qatar champion, with upside in London where World No. 2 Amina Orfi is defending champion). However, Orfi's overtake odds are materially higher than 0.23: she won the 2026 World Championships and British Open (beating El Hammamy), led the tour in % of points won (61.8% vs 59.6%), came within one match of #1 at June's Tour Finals, and PSA previews highlight Doha as her immediate shot at #1—especially with El Hammamy facing returning former #1 Nouran Gohar in the Qatar quarter-finals. Meanwhile, Gohar (returning at #6 seed after a 1-year absence, skipping London) has virtually no mathematical path to #1 by Sept 21, and Nour El Sherbini (skipping London, #3 seed in Qatar) has only a remote tail chance (0.015). Accordingly, we shift El Hammamy 0.72 -> 0.63, Orfi 0.23 -> 0.35, El Sherbini 0.03 -> 0.015, and drop Gohar.

questions.title: Which Ukrainian city away from the eastern and southern front lines will experience repeated Russian strikes on fuel stations by September 11, 2026?
questions.background: Russian attacks have repeatedly hit fuel stations near Ukraine’s eastern and southern battle lines. The spread of this targeting pattern to cities farther from the fighting would broaden its impact on civilians.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official Ukrainian municipal statements and reliable contemporaneous reporting citing local authorities. Resolution Conditions : Identify the Ukrainian city outside the eastern and southern frontline areas where Russian attacks are confirmed to have directly struck fuel stations on at least two separate days between September 1 and September 11, 2026. Reports of isolated attacks or incidental damage to nearby stations do not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the city.
questions.current_reasoning: Major breaking 2026-09-02 update from Interfax-Ukraine (11:59): Ukrnafta board chairman Bohdan Kukura confirmed an enemy Russian drone directly struck a UKRNAFTA gas station in Odesa region on Sept 2, effectively destroying the main building and canopy and severely damaging equipment. Local Sept 1-2 reporting (Straits Times/Reuters, Al Jazeera, Hindustan Times, Daily Beast) shows Odesa is under consecutive-night Russian jet-drone and missile barrages hitting energy and city targets (Sept 1 Naftogaz Odesa CHP and port facilities; Sept 2 174-drone barrage causing Odesa power outages and damaging a 24-story building) just as Putin vowed large-scale retaliatory strikes on Ukrainian energy facilities after Ukraine hit Ust-Luga. Odesa—unequivocally away from eastern/southern front lines—may already have Day 1 of the 2 separate days required during Sept 1-11 with 9 days remaining and is clearly an active Russian fuel-network target, lifting Odesa sharply (0.15 -> 0.38, kept well below 0.50 because Interfax specified 'Odesa region' rather than explicitly confirming Odesa city municipal limits and a second separate day is still needed). Scaling down other contenders proportionally while accounting for ongoing Sept 1-2 Russian strikes on Dnipro (0.20 -> 0.15) and Kyiv's seventh straight day of strikes (0.16 -> 0.13), along with Poltava (0.16 -> 0.11) and Chernihiv (0.11 -> 0.08) (sum = 0.85, leaving 0.15 for Sumy, Kryvyi Rih, and other rear cities).

questions.title: Which country will be the first in 2026 to publicly acknowledge deploying purpose-built weapons in Earth orbit?
questions.background: Military satellites provide communications, navigation and intelligence services. Deploying weapons in orbit could significantly change how countries protect or threaten these systems.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Public statements by national governments or military officials, corroborated by reliable international news reporting. Qualifying Event : Resolve to the country whose government or military first publicly acknowledges during 2026 that it has already deployed purpose-built weapons in Earth orbit. Merely describing satellites with potential military applications, announcing future deployments, or confirming ground-based anti-satellite weapons does not qualify. Resolution Timing : Resolve on the date of the first qualifying public acknowledgment, provided it occurs by December 31, 2026. Accepted Answer Format : The country's commonly used English name.
questions.current_reasoning: No country had publicly acknowledged already-deployed orbital weapons as of Aug 25, 2026. However, Aug 14 reporting (Asia Times / The War Zone) revealed a notable US doctrinal shift: US SPACECOM Commander Gen. Stephen Whiting announced offensive kinetic and non-kinetic ASAT capabilities ('integrated space fires' and counter-pLEO) as a top military priority, with US defense officials explicitly stressing the joint force must possess a 'credible, acknowledged ability' to attack adversary space assets (while noting the ground-based CCS jammer remains the only publicly acknowledged US offensive ASAT to date). Meanwhile, Aug 8 reporting on Golden Dome confirmed $3.2B for space-based interceptor prototypes targeting late-2026 tests and 2027 flight demos (future, not yet deployed). With Pentagon leadership openly building the case for public acknowledgment ahead of the mid-September AFA Air, Space & Cyber Conference, US probability rises from 0.42 to 0.49 while Russia (0.25, active co-orbital ASAT testing), China (0.12), France (0.08), and India (0.03) remain key alternatives.
